history.dynasty: Harichandan dynasty of Nilagiri (rediscovery); original builder disputed
history.period: Disputed: 12th or 13th century CE claimed; 19th-century rediscovery
history.summary: CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS (verify): one account dates the temple to the 13th century (attributed to Sivaramakesari, an ancestor of the local ruler), another to the 12th century CE (Eastern Ganga dynasty). The widely repeated local tradition holds that the site was rediscovered in the 19th century when Queen Arnapurna Devi of Nilagiri dreamt of the five Lingas, and King Krishna Chandra Mardaraj Harichandan unearthed and revived the shrine. Legend attributes the Lingas to Sita during Rama's exile, or to King Banasura. The temple's Lingas sit in a natural reservoir under a perennial stream flowing over them, and devotees lie flat on the rock to touch and worship them; the stream and an adjacent Banadevi shrine are noted by local sources. The original structure was reportedly damaged by flooding in 1820 and rebuilt in 1831. No verified archaeological dating found.

name: Panchalingeswar Temple
town_description: Nilagiri is a small historic town in Balasore district, Odisha, set at the foothills of the Swarnachuda hills about 17 km from Balasore. It was the seat of the Harichandan royal family, whose palace and gardens stand near the Jagannath Temple. The town is the gateway to nearby Panchalingeswar hill and attracts pilgrims and nature tourists year-round.
